test_cases.test_case: Rapid double-click Add to cart prevents duplicate additions
preconditions: User is logged in
Product Inventory page is visible
At least one product is shown with an "Add to cart" button and cart badge is visible
The selected product is not currently in the cart (button text = "Add to cart")
steps: 1. Locate a visible product item with an "Add to cart" button
2. Click the product's "Add to cart" button
3. Immediately click the product's "Add to cart" button again (single click)
test_cases.expected_result: First click succeeds and adds the item: the product button changes to "Remove" and the cart badge increments by one. The second click is ignored (no second addition); cart badge does not increment a second time and only one cart entry appears for the product (UI shows a single changed button to "Remove").

test_cases.test_case: Immediate toggle Add → Remove before UI update yields consistent final state
preconditions: User is logged in
Product Inventory page is visible
At least one product is shown with an "Add to cart" button and cart badge is visible
The selected product is not currently in the cart (button text = "Add to cart")
steps: 1. Locate a visible product item with an "Add to cart" button
2. Click the product's "Add to cart" button
3. Immediately (before visual state stabilizes) click the product's displayed "Remove" button (single click)
test_cases.expected_result: The sequence of rapid Add then Remove succeeds in producing a consistent final state: the product ends not in the cart (button shows "Add to cart") and the cart badge reflects the single net change (no phantom increments). There is no visible duplication of the item in the cart and the UI does not display an inconsistent intermediate state after actions complete.

test_cases.test_case: Repeated/rapid sort by Price (low–high) is deterministic (detect non-deterministic ordering)
preconditions: User is logged in
Product Inventory page is visible
At least five products are listed so ordering can be observed
Cart contents are irrelevant
steps: 1. Locate the sort dropdown on the Product Inventory page
2. Select the sort option Price (low–high)
3. Immediately re-select the sort option Price (low–high) (click) — repetition 1
4. Re-select the sort option Price (low–high) (click) — repetition 2
5. Re-select the sort option Price (low–high) (click) — repetition 3
6. Re-select the sort option Price (low–high) (click) — repetition 4
7. Observe and compare the visible product list order after each selection
test_cases.expected_result: Each sort action succeeds; the visible order of products after each repeated Price (low–high) selection is identical (deterministic). If any repetition yields a different visible order, that indicates non-deterministic sorting (test fails).

2. On the confirmation page, click the browser Back button
3. On the Checkout - Overview page, click the Finish button again
test_cases.expected_result: First click succeeds: order completes and confirmation page is shown. After navigating back, the second click is blocked / error shown: the application prevents creating a duplicate order (the UI either redirects back to the existing confirmation page or shows a visible message that resubmission is blocked). No duplicate confirmation is visible.

test_cases.test_case: Very long shipping address displayed on Overview (display/truncation/wrapping behavior)
preconditions: Cart contains at least one item
User has entered a shipping address containing a very long free-text string (very long, e.g., >200 characters) during earlier checkout steps
Payment information is set and visible on the Overview step
User navigates to the Checkout - Overview page
steps: 1. Observe the shipping address as displayed in the Overview page order summary/totals section
2. Click the Finish button
test_cases.expected_result: The Overview displays the very long shipping address (either wrapped across multiple lines or truncated with an ellipsis) with a visible UI indication (wrapped or truncated). No input validation error is shown for the long address. Clicking Finish succeeds: order completes and the confirmation page is shown.

test_cases.test_case: Confirmation page displays success message and Back Home button
preconditions: User logged in as <role>
User has completed checkout
steps: 1. Open the Checkout Confirmation page
2. Observe the page header and body
3. Verify the success message and primary actions are visible
test_cases.expected_result: Page displays "Thank you for your order!" and a visible 'Back Home' button is present on the Checkout Confirmation page

test_cases.test_case: Clicking Back Home returns to Product Inventory and clears the cart
preconditions: User logged in as <role>
User has completed checkout and is on the Checkout Confirmation page with items previously in the cart
steps: 1. Open the Checkout Confirmation page
2. Click the 'Back Home' button
test_cases.expected_result: Navigates to Product Inventory and clears the cart.

test_cases.test_case: Back Home click does not navigate away from Confirmation page
preconditions: User is on the Checkout Confirmation page after completing an order; confirmation message is visible; cart currently contains <items>
steps: 1. Click the 'Back Home' button on the Confirmation page
test_cases.expected_result: The action is blocked: the UI remains on the Checkout Confirmation page; the success message (e.g. 'Thank you for your order!') remains visible; Product Inventory page is NOT displayed; the cart badge still shows a <non-zero count> (cart was not cleared).

test_cases.test_case: Back Home navigates to Product Inventory but cart is not cleared
preconditions: User is on the Checkout Confirmation page after completing an order; confirmation message is visible; cart currently contains <items>
steps: 1. Click the 'Back Home' button on the Confirmation page
2. Observe the landing page after the click
test_cases.expected_result: Partial failure: Product Inventory page is displayed, but the cart was NOT cleared — the cart badge shows a <non-zero count> and previously ordered items remain in the cart. The on_success effect ('clears the cart') did not occur.

test_cases.test_case: Single Back Home click navigates to Product Inventory and clears cart
preconditions: User has items in cart
User completed checkout and is on the Confirmation page showing the success message
steps: 1. Click the "Back Home" button on the Confirmation page
test_cases.expected_result: Navigation to Product Inventory succeeds; Product Inventory page is displayed; cart badge/count shows 0 items and the cart contents view shows no items (cart cleared); the Confirmation page is no longer visible

test_cases.test_case: Rapid double-click of Back Home results in single successful navigation and cart cleared once
preconditions: User has items in cart
User completed checkout and is on the Confirmation page showing the success message
steps: 1. Click the "Back Home" button on the Confirmation page
2. Immediately click the "Back Home" button again before navigation completes
test_cases.expected_result: First click navigates to Product Inventory and succeeds; second click is ignored or has no adverse effect (no duplicate navigation or error shown); cart badge/count shows 0 items and cart contents are empty after navigation

test_cases.test_case: Back Home clicked from multiple open confirmation tabs: first clears cart, subsequent clicks navigate with empty cart
preconditions: User has items in cart
User completed checkout and opened the Confirmation page in two separate browser tabs (Tab A and Tab B), both showing the success message
steps: 1. In Tab A, click the "Back Home" button
2. In Tab B, click the "Back Home" button
test_cases.expected_result: First click (Tab A) navigates to Product Inventory and succeeds; cart badge/count becomes 0 and cart contents are cleared; second click (Tab B) also navigates to Product Inventory and succeeds but shows an already-empty cart (cart remains 0 items); no errors are shown and no items are re-added to the cart

test_cases.test_case: User clicks Logout and is returned to Login; protected pages become inaccessible
preconditions: User logged in as <role>
User is on a protected page (e.g., inventory or cart)
steps: 1. Click the Logout button in the application header
test_cases.expected_result: Ends the session and returns the user to the login page. After logout, protected pages (inventory, detail, cart, checkout) are not accessible without logging in again.

test_cases.test_case: Unauthenticated direct access to a protected page is blocked
preconditions: User is not authenticated (no active session)
steps: 1. In the browser address bar, navigate to the Inventory page URL (protected page)
test_cases.expected_result: User is redirected to the Login page; the Login form is displayed and the Inventory content is not rendered; no authenticated session is created (protected page remains inaccessible).

test_cases.test_case: Attempt to invoke Logout endpoint when not logged in
preconditions: User is not authenticated (no active session)
steps: 1. In the browser address bar, navigate to the Logout endpoint/URL (invoke logout) while not logged in
test_cases.expected_result: Application shows or redirects to the Login page (Login form visible); no server error is shown; no session was ended because none existed (action is effectively blocked).

test_cases.test_case: Using browser Back after logout does not reveal protected content
preconditions: User is authenticated (logged in as <role>)
steps: 1. Log in as <role>
2. Navigate to the Inventory page (protected)
3. Click the Logout control
4. After logout completes and Login page is shown, click the browser Back button
test_cases.expected_result: After pressing Back the Inventory page content is not displayed; the Login page is shown (or user is redirected to Login) and no protected content is visible; the user remains unauthenticated (session remains ended).

test_cases.test_case: Browser Back after Logout should not reveal protected page
preconditions: User is logged in
A protected page (inventory/detail/cart/checkout) is open in the current tab
steps: 1. Click the Logout button
2. Wait for the app to return to the login page
3. Click the browser Back button
test_cases.expected_result: Attempt to navigate back to the protected page is blocked / error shown: the app shows the login page and protected page content is not displayed

test_cases.test_case: Refresh a protected page in a second tab after logging out in the first tab
preconditions: User is logged in
Protected page is open in Tab B
An active session exists in Tab A
steps: 1. In Tab A click the Logout button
2. In Tab B click the browser Refresh button / Reload
test_cases.expected_result: Refresh of the protected page is blocked / error shown: Tab B is redirected to the login page and protected content is not accessible without logging in again

test_cases.test_case: Rapid repeated clicks on Logout do not create inconsistent session state
preconditions: User is logged in
A protected page is open
steps: 1. Click the Logout button
2. Immediately click the Logout button again
test_cases.expected_result: First logout succeeds: user is redirected to the login page; the second click has no adverse effect and no additional sessions or errors are created (user remains on login page)

test_cases.test_case: Reset clears cart and resets UI states without logging out
preconditions: User logged in as <role>
Cart contains one or more <items>; cart badge is visible; items that are in the cart display the 'Remove' button state
steps: 1. On the app main screen, click the 'Reset App State' control
2. Wait for the UI to refresh
test_cases.expected_result: Cart list shows no items; the cart badge is no longer visible; product tiles that previously displayed 'Remove' now display the 'Add' button state; the user remains logged in (account avatar or account menu remains visible).

test_cases.test_case: After Reset the user stays logged in and can add items again
preconditions: User logged in as <role>
Cart contains one or more <items> before reset; add/remove buttons reflect added items
steps: 1. On the app main screen, click the 'Reset App State' control
2. Wait for the UI to refresh
3. Click 'Add' on a product tile to add it to the cart
test_cases.expected_result: User remains logged in after reset and is able to add items: the selected product appears in the cart list and the cart badge becomes visible again reflecting the added item(s).

test_cases.test_case: Unauthenticated user attempts to invoke Reset App State
preconditions: User is not authenticated (not logged in)
steps: 1. Navigate to the application page that contains the Reset App State control
2. Click the 'Reset App State' control
test_cases.expected_result: Navigation is redirected to the Login page; the Reset action is blocked (no cart clearing or UI state reset). The cart contents remain unchanged (<cart contents> remains visible) and the user is not logged in.

test_cases.test_case: User with a role that lacks permission cannot see or use Reset App State
preconditions: User is authenticated as <unauthorized role> (a role that should not perform Reset App State)
steps: 1. Sign in as <unauthorized role>
2. Navigate to the application page that normally contains the Reset App State control
3. Inspect the page for the presence of the 'Reset App State' control
test_cases.expected_result: The 'Reset App State' control is not visible or is disabled for <unauthorized role>; no Reset action can be performed. The cart and UI state remain unchanged (cart badge and add/remove button states are unchanged).

test_cases.test_case: Rapid repeated clicks on Reset App State button
preconditions: User is logged in and visible in the UI (profile avatar or sign-out link present)
Cart contains at least one item and the cart badge shows a non-zero count
Reset App State control/button is visible
steps: 1. Click the Reset App State button
2. Immediately click the Reset App State button again (within 1 second)
test_cases.expected_result: Reset action succeeds: cart is cleared (cart list empty) and cart badge shows zero; no duplicate errors or multiple-clear side-effects are shown; add/remove button states reset to default; user remains logged in (profile avatar and sign-out link remain visible)

test_cases.test_case: Click Reset App State while on the in-progress checkout page
preconditions: User is logged in and visible in the UI (profile avatar or sign-out link present)
User is on the checkout page with items in the cart and the checkout form (Place order or equivalent) visible
steps: 1. Click the Reset App State button
test_cases.expected_result: Reset action succeeds: cart is cleared and cart badge shows zero; checkout UI reflects empty cart (checkout form shows a 'cart is empty' message or the Place order button is disabled/inactive); user remains logged in (profile avatar and sign-out link remain visible)

test_cases.test_case: Reset App State in one browser tab updates another open tab without manual refresh
preconditions: User is logged in and visible in the UI (profile avatar or sign-out link present)
Two browser tabs are open to the app under the same user account (Tab A and Tab B)
Both tabs show the cart with at least one item and a non-zero cart badge
steps: 1. In Tab A, click the Reset App State button
2. In Tab B, observe the cart UI without performing a manual refresh
test_cases.expected_result: Reset action in Tab A succeeds: cart is cleared in Tab A and cart badge shows zero; Tab B updates automatically (cart list empty and cart badge shows zero) without manual refresh; user remains logged in in both tabs (profile avatar and sign-out link remain visible)
